module_catalog.name: Academic information management 111
module_catalog.content: Find, evaluate, process, manage and present information resources for academic purposes using appropriate technology.
module_catalog.service_modules: Faculty of Engineering, Built Environment and Information Technology Faculty of Education Faculty of Economic and Management Sciences Faculty of Humanities Faculty of Law Faculty of Health Sciences Faculty of Natural and Agricultural Sciences Faculty of Theology and Religion

module_catalog.name: Academic information management 121
module_catalog.content: Apply effective search strategies in different technological environments. Demonstrate the ethical and fair use of information resources. Integrate 21st-century communications into the management of academic information.
module_catalog.service_modules: Faculty of Engineering, Built Environment and Information Technology Faculty of Education Faculty of Economic and Management Sciences Faculty of Humanities Faculty of Law Faculty of Health Sciences Faculty of Natural and Agricultural Sciences Faculty of Theology and Religion Faculty of Veterinary Science

module_catalog.name: Anatomy 111
module_catalog.content: Anatomy for communication pathology This module is on the theory and practical experience of the structure of the organs involved with speech production and hearing excluding neuro-anatomy. Anatomical terminology and elementary study of tissues; gross anatomy of structures involved with speech production and hearing: larynx, skeletal components and muscles involved with respiration, viscera of the respiratory system, bones and paranasal sinuses of the skull, synopsis of the cranial nerves, structure of the viscera of the vocal tract, structure of the ear; embryology of the face, palate, tongue, larynx and ear.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 lectures per week, 1 practical per week

module_catalog.name: Physiology 110
module_catalog.content: Introduction (terminology and anatomical orientation); chemical principles; cytology and histology; neuro-physiology and the senses; haematology and body fluids; cardiovascular system.
module_catalog.service_modules: Faculty of Humanities Faculty of Natural and Agricultural Sciences

module_catalog.name: Physiology 120
module_catalog.content: Respiratory system; nutrition; digestion and metabolism; kidneys and acid-base equilibrium; endocrinology; reproduction physiology and reproduction; skin and body temperatures.
module_catalog.service_modules: Faculty of Humanities Faculty of Natural and Agricultural Sciences

module_catalog.name: Integrated healthcare leadership 120
module_catalog.content: Leadership and multidisciplinary teamwork. Healthcare systems and legislation. Determinants of health. Introduction to healthcare models (e.g. community-based care, family-centred care, etc.). Professionalism, Ethical principles. Management of diversity.

module_catalog.name: People and their environment 112
module_catalog.content: This module comprises basic psychology and sociology concepts relevant to medicine, and to dentistry, in the case of BChD students. Basic psychiatric concepts are also taught.
module_catalog.service_modules: Faculty of Health Sciences Faculty of Natural and Agricultural Sciences

module_catalog.name: Sepedi for beginners 119
module_catalog.content: *For absolute beginners only. * Students from the School of Healthcare Sciences and the School of Dentistry, who already possess the language skills taught in this module, may write an exemption examination. The acquisition of basic Sepedi communicative skills with emphasis on everyday expressions and suitable high frequency vocabulary, within specific social situations.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 lectures per week, 1 discussion class per week

module_catalog.name: Typical language development 110
module_catalog.content: Typical language development across the lifespan, from prenatal language learning to infancy, the toddler years, preschool and school-age language and literacy development, and adolescent and adult language use. Factors influencing language development.

module_catalog.name: Introduction to the auditory system 111
module_catalog.content: The anatomy and physiology of the auditory system, common hearing disorders, and the perceptual aspects of sound. Introduction to audiological screening practices and principles. Overview of amplification (theory and practical application), role of aural rehabilitation and related assessment strategies. Introduction to audiological assessment procedures including the audiometric test battery, pure-tone audiometry, speech audiometry, and immittance testing. Overview of the principles underlying these assessments and a foundational knowledge of amplification devices.

module_catalog.name: Speech sound disorders and craniofacial disorders 120
module_catalog.content: Introduction to communication disorders. Theoretical principles of assessment and intervention in communication disorders; basic assessment protocol; procedures and techniques. Introduction to ethical principles and standards. The theoretical underpinnings of prevention and early identification of speech, language, and hearing disorders within educational and healthcare contexts. Introduction to assessment and intervention approaches for speech sound disorders as well as ethical considerations in the field. The specific characteristics and nature of speech sound and craniofacial disorders, including an overview of orofacial myofunctional disorders and teratogens. Etiology of communication difficulties; introduction to genetics.

module_catalog.name: Introduction to management of communication disorders: Practicum 181
module_catalog.content: Introduction to communication disorders. Overview of the theoretical frameworks, as well as practical application thereof for assessment and intervention. Applied ethical principles and standards for service delivery including person-centred care and cultural humility. Practical exposure to normal communication development and hearing screening. Introduction to acoustic phonetics and applied perceptual analysis of speech. Practical exposure through observation of SSD therapy and early communication intervention at clinical placements.

module_catalog.name: Communication processes and introduction to linguistics 110
module_catalog.content: Overview of linguistics, exploring the nature of language, speech, and communication.  Application of theory to linguistic concepts including pragmatics, semantics, syntax, morphology, and phonology. Overview of normal receptive and expressive language processes.

module_catalog.name: Speech acoustics 120
module_catalog.content: Introduction to the physics of sound as it relates to speech production. Overview of speech acoustics, including resonance and its application to speech production. Practical experience in speech sound analysis through the use of speech sound spectrography.

module_catalog.name: Introduction to articulatory phonetics 181
module_catalog.content: Introduction to articulatory phonetics and AI in speech-language pathology, including AI-powered automatic speech recognition and acoustic analysis tools. The speech communication process – production phase. The speech organs: position and function. Different airstream mechanisms, consonant table, articulatory and perceptual characteristics of consonants, including phonetic symbols and diacritics.

module_catalog.name: Setswana for beginners 110
module_catalog.content: * For absolute beginners only. The acquisition of basic Setswana communicative skills with emphasis on everyday expressions and suitable high frequency vocabulary within specific social situations.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 lectures per week, 1 discussion class per week

module_catalog.name: isiZulu for beginners 119
module_catalog.content: *For absolute beginners only * Students from the School of Healthcare Sciences, who already possess the language skills taught in this module, may write an exemption examination. The acquisition of basic isiZulu communicative skills with emphasis on everyday expressions and suitable high frequency vocabulary, within specific situations.
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 lectures per week, 1 discussion class per week

module_catalog.name: Integrated healthcare leadership 210
module_catalog.content: This module aims to enhance integrated healthcare leadership through interprofessional teamwork in the context of community health. The focus is especially on communication skills, project development and health promotion. The theory is applied in a health education needs/strength analysis.
module_catalog.prerequisites: IHL 120 (For Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology, Physiotherapy and Dietetics students only IHL 120 is applicable).
module_catalog.contact_time: 2 lectures per week, 4 practicals per week

module_catalog.name: Neuro-anatomy for communication pathology 211
module_catalog.content: This module focuses on the theory and practical experience of the structure of the central nervous system, course and distribution of the cranial nerves and embryology of the central nervous system. Division; embryology of the central nervous system; histology of the nervous system; gross anatomy: spinal cord, brain stem, cerebral hemispheres, ventricles, meninges and circulation of cerebro-spinal fluid, blood circulation, cranial nerves, autonomic nervous system and tracts of the CNS.
module_catalog.contact_time: 1 lecture per week, 1 practical per week

module_catalog.name: Neuro-physiology 221
module_catalog.content: Neuronal physiology, central nervous system, peripheral nervous system, including the afferent and efferent divisions.

module_catalog.name: Language disorders and learning disorders 210
module_catalog.content: Introduction to the nature, causes, and characteristics of various developmental language and learning disorders. Approaches to assessment and intervention including strategies for these disorders and language sample analysis. Second language acquisition and characteristics of learners in and additional language learning environment.

module_catalog.name: Aural rehabilitation across the lifespan 211
module_catalog.content: Aural rehabilitation for infants, children and adults with hearing loss: assessment, intervention components, services and the shared role of the speech-language therapist and audiologist.

module_catalog.name: Pediatric neurocommunicative disorders 220
module_catalog.content: Introduction to pediatric neurocommunicative disorders, including cerebral palsy, pediatric traumatic brain injury, childhood dysarthria, and childhood apraxia of speech, as well as neurodevelopmental disorders such as Autism. Overview of the nature, causes, and characteristics of these disorders, as well as assessment and intervention strategies, including interprofessionalism. Introduction to the complexities of communication for individuals with complex communication needs, focusing on augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) systems and strategies. Assessment, implementation, and feature matching of AAC devices and systems, as well as the application of unaided communication methods.

module_catalog.name: Neuromotor speech disorders, voice disorders and fluency disorders 220
module_catalog.content: A comprehensive overview of neuromotor speech disorders, focusing on adult populations delving into the nature, causes, and characteristics of various disorders, including acquired dysarthria, acquired apraxia of speech. A comprehensive overview of paediatric and adult dysphagia fluency disorders, and voice disorders. Exploring evidence-based approaches to assessment and intervention strategies for these disorders.

module_catalog.name: Early communication intervention and auditory processing disorder 222
module_catalog.content: Early communication intervention for infants and toddlers at risk of communication delay or disorders. Principles and approaches, description of risk populations, screening, assessment and intervention of infants and toddlers at risk of communication delay, including caregiver education. Neurodevelopmental supportive care and neonatal communication intervention. The nature, causes, and characteristics of auditory processing disorder, encompassing organic and non-organic factors, assessment, intervention, and the role of a transdisciplinary approach.

module_catalog.name: Speech sound, craniofacial, language, and learning disorders: Practicum 281
module_catalog.content: Semester 1: Screening, assessment of and intervention with clients of all ages with speech sound and cranio-facial disorders in education, work and social contexts. Counselling of these clients and their significant others. Participation in teamwork. Understanding of the principles of assessment, intervention, professional ethics, evidence-based practice and clinical report writing through seminars. Semester 2: Screening, assessment of and intervention with clients with various developmental language and learning disorders in education, work, and social contexts. Collaboration with and counselling of these clients and their significant others. Participation in teamwork. Understanding and application of the principles of assessment, intervention, professional ethics, evidence-based practice and clinical report writing through seminars. Guided observation at a voice clinic and Facial Cleft Deformities Clinic.

module_catalog.name: Integrated healthcare leadership 310
module_catalog.content: Community needs assessment. Leadership in community development. Planning and implementation of collaborative community-based interventions. Application of principles of monitoring and evaluation. NB: Only for School of Healthcare Sciences and Department of Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology students.

module_catalog.name: Neurogenic communication disorders and dysphagia in adult populations 310
module_catalog.content: Exploration of acquired neurogenic communication disorders (including aphasia and traumatic brain injury) and adult dysphagia.   Focusing on the nature and implications for individuals and their families, causal factors, evidence-based assessment and intervention practices.
module_catalog.prerequisites: SLP 210, SLP 211, SLP 220, SLP 221, SLP 222, SLP 281, NFG 221, NAN 211.

module_catalog.name: Cognitive-communication disorders and dysphagia arising from neurodegenerative disorders 320
module_catalog.content: Overview of progressive neurodegenerative disorders impacting cognitive-communication functions and swallowing. Exploring conditions such as primary progressive aphasia, dementia, and Parkinson's disease, examining their nature, causal factors, and associated challenges. Discuss the unique characteristics of individuals with these disorders, including cognitive impairments, communication difficulties, and dysphagia. Highlighting evidence-based approaches to assessment and intervention, tailored to address the evolving needs of individuals with progressive neurodegenerative.
module_catalog.prerequisites: SLP 210, SLP 211, SLP 220, SLP 221, SLP 222, SLP 281, NFG 221, NAN 211.

module_catalog.name: Pediatric swallowing and feeding disorders 321
module_catalog.content: Description of dysphagia in infants and children. Nature and causal factors of pediatric dysphagia. Approaches to assessment and intervention. Advanced theory, recent research and issues in neonatal and pediatric dysphagia. Challenges posed to professional practice in the local context.
module_catalog.prerequisites: SLP 210, SLP 211, SLP 220, SLP 221, SLP 222, SLP 281, NFG 221, NAN 211.

module_catalog.name: Language disorders and complex communication disorders: Practicum 381
module_catalog.content: Assessment, intervention, and management of individuals with various child-language and learning disorders, ADHD, autism, voice and fluency disorders in children. Development of clinical skills through practical experience, including guided observation in a voice clinic and placements in mainstream and LSEN educational settings as well as care centres. Collaboration, counselling, and teamwork while incorporating theoretical frameworks such as evidence-based practice, ethics, and report writing. Exposure to voice, fluency, AAC, adult neurogenic disorders, and pediatric dysphagia. Practical language sample analysis and augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) practices in different supportive contexts. Seminars exploring the secondary professional functions of audiologists and speech-language pathologists in developing countries, including consultation, counselling, education, management, and medico-legal responsibilities. Experiential learning to enhance clinical competence and professional development in administrative, financial and business management.
module_catalog.prerequisites: SLP 210, SLP 211, SLP 220, SLP 221, SLP 222, SLP 281

module_catalog.name: Interprofessional community-based engagements: Practicum 382
module_catalog.content: Application of interprofessional education and collaborative practice (IPECP) core competencies by speech-language pathology students during community engagements with interprofessional teams. Experiential learning in a public hospital and neonatal communication intervention in practice. Seminars in Aural (re)habilitation and early communication intervention. Guided observations at the Clinic for High-Risk Babies as well as peadiatric parent guidance as part of aural (re)habilitation.
module_catalog.prerequisites: SLP 210, SLP 211, SLP 220, SLP 221, SLP 222, SLP 281

module_catalog.name: Research fundamentals for speech-language pathology 383
module_catalog.content: Introduction to the fundamental concepts and processes of research. Critical stages of research, including formulating research ideas, developing research questions, conducting literature reviews, and designing research proposals. Appraising existing research studies, apply research principles, design and write a proposal. Research ethics and use of AI in research.
module_catalog.prerequisites: SLP 210, SLP 211, SLP 220, SLP 221, SLP 222, SLP 281
